notes.title: Version 2.2 Update
notes.content:
[h1]Version 2.2 Update[/h1]
Issues addressed in this version:
[list]
[*] Fixed a very time-specific, opponent and player moves-specific issue that happened only in [b]Classic[/b] mode, when the opponent's move became invisible if the player spammed the board with clicks while it was the opponent's turn.
[/list]

[h1]Note[/h1]
The first time that this issue surfaced, it was presented as a screenshot in the [b]Screenshots[/b] forum, by a user which also uploaded fake data to the leaderboards and was VAC banned by Steam in other games. Because of this, I haven't followed up on the issue then, since I thought that the respective user hacked the game and I figured it uploaded the image as a fake. Then other similar screenshots appeared and I started investigating, though I couldn't reproduce the issue. Being only two or three such screenshots, without a clear description on how the problem arose, I haven't investigated too much into this, since I thought that these images might also be fake. However, in time, these screenshots started appearing more and more and I've also seen a youtube video where a user recorded the issue happening. Then, after intense tests where I couldn't reproduce the bug, I contacted all the users that uploaded the screenshots, in order to get more information. Alas, two of them really helped me out by describing how they caught the bug and I was able to reproduce it, then, myself. It was hard because it's very time-specific and it's also specific to the way the players place their game pieces and one of the players has to spam the board with clicks while it's the opponent's turn. The issue has been fixed now, but I just want to stress on the fact that users that behave badly (uploading fake scores and using cheats), makes it harder for everyone else to get a good game, since I could have followed on the issue and fixed it way sooner. So, if you want to cheat, not caring about the people that made a game, fine, but please also think about your fellow players, you're making it harder for everyone else to have a nice experience with the respective game, so please be considerate and think twice before doing that, and hopefully you won't destroy every other player's joy of the game. Also, if you spot a problem, please add a little description on how you encountered that problem, it will help fix it. Thank you!

notes.title: Version 2.1 Update
notes.content:
[h1]Version 2.1 Update[/h1]
Issues addressed in this version:
[list]
[*] Added back the rule where, if a player has an [b]Infinite[/b] turn time set, but the other has any other turn time set, it defaults to [b]30s[/b]. This will prevent people from not making a move when they know they're going to lose. The other rules remain the same: turn time will be [b]Infinite[/b] if both players have [b]Infinite[/b] turn times set, other than that, the most forgiving of the two options will be enabled, for example, if one player has [b]10s[/b] set and the other [b]5s[/b], then the turn time will be set to [b]10s[/b].
[/list]
[h1]Note[/h1]

Version 2.0 update broke compatibility with [b]Windows Vista[/b], since it added support for touch-enabled devices. However, no one reported this issue, and, on the other hand, touch support was happily welcomed, so I'll leave it as is.

[h1]One Month Celebration[/h1]

One month ago, on the 28th of April, the game launched on Steam. It was Greenlit with over 1.200 votes and since its launch it has been played by over 100.000 people. To celebrate, I would like to share with you this awesome [url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=h_LvOTdXOTU]review[/url] that [b]Kevin[/b] made. [i]Thanks, Kevin! :)[/i]

[b]Thank you all for playing![/b]

notes.title: Version 1.9 Update
notes.content:
[h1]Version 1.9 Update[/h1]
Issues addressed in this version:
[list]
[*] When turn time expires, the opponent can move anywhere he wants. [i]This way the players won't enter into a gridlock where, if one makes a move, the other will win the match and they'll indefinitely wait for each other to make the losing move.[/i]
[*] If at least one of the players has [b]Infinite[/b] selected as [b]Turn Time[/b], then the game turn time will default to [b]Infinite[/b], [b]not[/b] 30s, as in the previous version, 1.8.
[*] When it's the AI's turn to play, because the player hasn't made a move in the designated time, the AI will be delayed for about 1 second to prevent the screen from flashing the AI's color and make for a smoother game transition.
[/list]
[h1]Note[/h1]
[b]Thanks for playing[/b] and, as always, please report any issues in the [b]Community Forums[/b].
[b]Enjoy![/b]

notes.title: Version 1.8 Update
notes.content:
[h1]Version 1.8 Update[/h1]
Issues addressed in this version:
[list]
[*] Added timed turns, based on players choices.
[*] Guard against connection time-outs when players do not have any turn time limit set. Initially the servers were timing-out if no player made a move in over 2 minutes.
[/list]
[h1]Timed turns[/h1]
Players can select in the [b]Options[/b] menu, from the following [b]Turn Time[/b] categories:
[list]
[*] [b]Infinite[/b]: No turn time limit. If in a [b]Multiplayer[/b] game the opponent has a time limit set, then the most permissive, of [b]30s[/b], will be selected by default ([i]otherwise the turn time will be [b]Infinite[/b][/i]).
[*] [b]30s[/b]: 30 seconds turn time limit. If the player doesn't make a move in this amount of time, the move will be given to the other player.
[*] [b]10s[/b]: 10 seconds turn time limit.
[*] [b]5s[/b]: 5 seconds turn time limit, for [i]hardcore[/i] players.
[/list]
In a [b]Multiplayer[/b] game, when both players have turn time limits set, the most permissive of the two will be selected by default, where the most permissive means the longest amount of time from the two options, for example: 1st player has [b]30s[/b], the 2nd [b]5s[/b] selected, then the turn play time will be of [b]30s[/b].

[h1]Note[/h1]
Thank you for playing and please report any issues in the [b]Community Forums[/b].
[b]Happy gaming![/b]

[list]

Most important issues that will be addressed in future updates:

notes.title: Version 1.6 Update
notes.content:
[h1]Version 1.6 Update[/h1]
Issues addressed in this version:
[list]
[*] A school bell will be heard whenever an opponent connects in a [i]Multiplayer Steam[/i] game, even though the game window is unselected. The window also flashes as the sound is played. (This will help you know when an opponent has connected to your game after a longer waiting time, where you could do something else in another application until a player is found). The waiting for game start information message may still be displayed for a couple of seconds after the sound is played, until the connection is validated and the game started.
[*] Alternating game piece in [i]Multiplayer[/i] games. When playing several games with the same user, you will both take turns into playing with X and O.
[*] Added [i]Bookworm[/i] achievement decimals. The displayed percentage is no longer rounded to 70% when it is under, but close to this value.
[*] Separated the menu sounds from the in-game sounds, as an entry in the [i]Options[/i] menu.
[*] Added click sounds for the [i]Yes[/i] and [i]No[/i] confirmation buttons.
[/list]

[h1]Future Updates[/h1]
Known issues that will be addressed in future updates:
[list]
[*] Make current active board(s) and hinted board(s) when the user hovers small board squares more obvious.
[*] Pulsating active board(s).
[*] Timed turns.
[*] AI to take over disconnected players.
[*] Display game mode above opponent's name in the top right corner of the game board.
[*] [b]Bug[/b]: If sound is unavailable system-wide, the game won't start.
[*] [b]Bug[/b]: An opponent may disconnect for a second, then reconnect and still be able to play, though his name will not be shown in the top right corner of the game board.
[/list]

Thanks for your support and happy gaming! ːrufusjokingː

notes.title: The clock is tic-tac-toe-ing...
notes.content:
Hello, all you happy people!

With almost a day until release, I just want to go over some of the game's feats:

[h1]Game modes[/h1]
[list]
[*] [b]Classic[/b] - A 3x3 board. Simple, cute, effective and down to earth. :)
[*] [b]Classic Forget[/b] - A 3x3 board, with a bit of a twist: the oldest 4th move of the same piece gets [i]forgotten[/i]. This way, a max of only 3 board pieces of the same type will ever be on the board. No more games that end in ties; you can trick your opponent into losing... if he doesn't trick you first.
[*] [b]Ultimate[/b] - Each square in a big 3x3 board contains another 3x3, smaller, board. You can only place your game piece in a smaller board. The square where you put your piece activates the big square of the big board and your opponent will have to play on the small board that is contained in that big square. When you win a small board, the big square that contains that board will be filled with your game piece. To win the big board and the game, you must fill 3-in-a-row big squares ([i]the same rule as winning a small board, actually[/i]). Be careful, though, if you send your opponent to an already filled big square (beit won by any of the two players or containing a filled small board - a draw board), then the opponent can choose to play in any big square that he likes. A draw square does not count for any of the players. The small board(s) where any of the players must make their move on will lit up in that player's game piece color: blue for X, red for O. If you hover any of the squares of the small board, the corresponding small board(s) where your opponent will play next will be hinted, by slightly lighting it/them up in your opponent's color. This way, you will always know in what big square(s) your opponent will make his next move.
[*] [b]Ultimate Forget[/b] - Same as [i]Ultimate[/i], only that each 4th oldest move of the same player will be [i]forgotten[/i], but only in the small boards. The big board is not affected by this [i]forgetful[/i] nature, so you can have more big squares filled with the same game piece. This eliminates the possibility that any of the small boards ends up in a draw.
[*] [b]Ultimate Forget Total[/b] - Same as [i]Ultimate Forget[/i], only that the big board is also affected by the 4th oldest game piece will be [i]forgotten[/i] rule. This way, not even the big board could end up in a tie. One player must be the victor, there's no other way around it. :)
[/list]

[h1]Player levels[/h1]
[list]
[*] Each player will be [b]ranked[/b], based on a [i]level system[/i]. This [i]level system[/i] is active only in [i]Ultimate[/i] type games, [i]single[/i] or [i]multi[/i] player, but not in [i]hot seat[/i] games. This way, no one can play against himself and rank up or down by winning or losing. It also gets past these questions: who won, who lost? The player on which account the game is running or his buddy, sitting next to him?
[*] The [b]maximum level[/b] a player can reach is [i]50[/i]. You also get a nice [i]achievement[/i] when [b]and if[/b] you reach this rank.
[*] [b]Levels 0 to 20[/b]: game win: +1, game lose: -1, game draw: 0, in rank.
[*] [b]Levels 21 to 35[/b]: game win: +1, game lose: -2, game draw: 0, in rank.
[*] [b]Levels 36 to 50[/b]: game win: +1, game lose: -2, game draw: -1, in rank.
[/list]

[h1]Tips and tricks[/h1]
[list]
[*] The [b]game piece[/b] can be changed in the [i]Options[/i] menu. You can choose to play with X or, hold on to your hats, O. I know, surprisingly!
[*] The player with the X piece will always [b]start first[/b].
[*] In [b]Multiplayer LAN[/b], the [i]server[/i] decides which game type to play and which game piece to use.
[*] In [b]Multiplayer Steam[/b], based on [i]random opponent[/i] matchmaking, the game server will try to match appropriate player levels, so you can play with people closer to your skill level. This does not eliminate the possibility to play with a higher or lower in rank opponent, based on how many players are actively searching for a skills-based match at that time, and what their rank is.
[*] Still in [b]Multiplayer Steam[/b], when playing with a [i]random opponent[/i], you may have to wait a little when the [i]"Waiting for opponent..."[/i] message appears. It means a game server of the chosen game type has been created and you're waiting for another player that has chosen the same game type to join your match. If there already is a game server of the chosen game type available (when you chose [i]random opponent[/i]), then you will just connect to that server instead.
[*] When you play a [b]multiplayer[/b] game, your [i]game piece[/i] can change, which will be reflected in the [i]Options[/i] menu. So if you usually play with X, but in a [i]multiplayer[/i] game you're designated to play with O, then, to suggest to the game that you'd prefer X for the next game (or when switching to [i]singleplayer[/i]), you must chose X again in the [i]Options[/i] menu.
[*] When you want to [b]restart[/b] a multiplayer game, your opponent must confirm this decision. He could chose to deny it, in which case you may ask again, but if he still denies it, you can't ask again. This avoids spamming the opponent, when you know you're going to lose. Act like a man and accept your loss. Hey! Maybe next match you'll dominate him and you wouldn't like it if he spammed you with game restart requests, would you?
[*] The [b]restart[/b] request feature works on a [i]ticketing[/i] system. When you start a new game, you start with two tickets. When you make a restart request, a ticket is consumed. When an opponent agrees to a request, your ticket will be returned to you. Whenever the opponent requests a restart, you will gain a ticket, but you can't hold more than two.
[*] When you [b]quit[/b] a multiplayer game, you will first be asked if you're sure you want to do that, because it will count as a loss for you. This avoids players quitting when they know they are going to lose and don't want to go down in rank. The rank will be affected anyway, so just let the opponent bask in his glory, you wouldn't want him to quit when it's your turn to bask in your glory, now would you? And don't even think of closing the game, either, your rank will still be affected, so just take both glory and loss as a real man!
[*] After a [b]game is over[/b], either players can start a new game. If your opponent starts a new game and places his piece on the board, but you don't want to play anymore, you can freely quit the game before placing your first game pice on the board, without suffering any penalty for doing so.
[/list]

Wow, now that was a long read!
If you've skipped some sections or just browsed through, don't worry, the game tries to make everything as seamless and easy as possible, so you can pick it up and play immediately...

Soon! :)

Hello, all you happy people!

With almost a day until release, I just want to go over some of the game's feats:

[h1]Game modes[/h1]
[list]
[*] [b]Classic[/b] - A 3x3 board. Simple, cute, effective and down to earth. :)
[*] [b]Classic Forget[/b] - A 3x3 board, with a bit of a twist: the oldest 4th move of the same piece gets [i]forgotten[/i]. This way, a max of only 3 board pieces of the same type will ever be on the board. No more games that end in ties; you can trick your opponent into losing... if he doesn't trick you first.
[*] [b]Ultimate[/b] - Each square in a big 3x3 board contains another 3x3, smaller, board. You can only place your game piece in a smaller board. The square where you put your piece activates the big square of the big board and your opponent will have to play on the small board that is contained in that big square. When you win a small board, the big square that contains that board will be filled with your game piece. To win the big board and the game, you must fill 3-in-a-row big squares ([i]the same rule as winning a small board, actually[/i]). Be careful, though, if you send your opponent to an already filled big square (beit won by any of the two players or containing a filled small board - a draw board), then the opponent can choose to play in any big square that he likes. A draw square does not count for any of the players. The small board(s) where any of the players must make their move on will lit up in that player's game piece color: blue for X, red for O. If you hover any of the squares of the small board, the corresponding small board(s) where your opponent will play next will be hinted, by slightly lighting it/them up in your opponent's color. This way, you will always know in what big square(s) your opponent will make his next move.
[*] [b]Ultimate Forget[/b] - Same as [i]Ultimate[/i], only that each 4th oldest move of the same player will be [i]forgotten[/i], but only in the small boards. The big board is not affected by this [i]forgetful[/i] nature, so you can have more big squares filled with the same game piece. This eliminates the possibility that any of the small boards ends up in a draw.
[*] [b]Ultimate Forget Total[/b] - Same as [i]Ultimate Forget[/i], only that the big board is also affected by the 4th oldest game piece will be [i]forgotten[/i] rule. This way, not even the big board could end up in a tie. One player must be the victor, there's no other way around it. :)
[/list]

[h1]Player levels[/h1]

[*] Each player will be [b]ranked[/b], based on a [i]level system[/i]. This [i]level system[/i] is active only in [i]Ultimate[/i] type games, [i]single[/i] or [i]multi[/i] player, but not in [i]hot seat[/i] games. This way, no one can play against himself and rank up or down by winning or losing. It also gets past these questions: who won, who lost? The player on which account the game is running or his buddy, sitting next to him?
[*] The [b]maximum level[/b] a player can reach is [i]50[/i]. You also get a nice [i]achievement[/i] when [b]and if[/b] you reach this rank.
[*] [b]Levels 0 to 20[/b]: game win: +1, game lose: -1, game draw: 0, in rank.
[*] [b]Levels 21 to 35[/b]: game win: +1, game lose: -2, game draw: 0, in rank.
[*] [b]Levels 36 to 50[/b]: game win: +1, game lose: -2, game draw: -1, in rank.
[/list]

[h1]Tips and tricks[/h1]
[list]
[*] The [b]game piece[/b] can be changed in the [i]Options[/i] menu. You can choose to play with X or, hold on to your hats, O. I know, surprisingly!

notes.title: Coming Sooner
notes.content:
[b]Good news, everyone![/b]

I've worked really hard lately and I've been able to integrate the game with Steam and also develop a new game mode: [b]Ultimate Forget Total[/b], and thus move the release date one week sooner, on the [b]28th of April[/b], 11:00 AM PST. Until then, I will debug the game extensively and see if there are any issues that need fixing until the big day arrives.

Here's a [b]rundown[/b] of what was promised in [b]Greenlight[/b] and what will be [b]released[/b]:
[list]
[*] [i]Promised:[/i] [b]Classic[/b] and [b]Ultimate[/b] game types. [i]Delivered[/i], including 2 more variations: [b]Forget[/b] and [b]Forget Total[/b].
[*] [i]Promised:[/i] [b]Single-player[/b], [b]Hot-seat[/b], [b]Multiplayer[/b] through [b]LAN[/b] and [b]Steam[/b]. [i]Delivered[/i].
[*] [i]Promised:[/i] 3 levels of [b]difficulty[/b]. [i]Delivered[/i].
[*] [i]Promised:[/i] [b]Rankings[/b], [b]Leaderboards[/b] and [b]Achievements[/b]. [i]Delivered[/i].
[*] [i]Extra:[/i] Hovering the play board will display a hint on where the opponent will be sent next.
[/list]

[b]Thanks[/b] for your interest and patience, soon you will be able to enjoy the game!

notes.title: Coming Soon
notes.content:
Hello, world!

The game will be available for download and free to play starting on the [b]5th of May PDT[/b].

The [b]achievements[/b] and [b]leaderboards[/b] have been implemented and are working as expected, the next step is to provide [i]matchmaking[/i] capabilities through the Steam interface. [b]LAN[/b] is already available and working fine, if anyone will prefer to play it this way, once it's launched.

Also, to celebrate the game being released and award all of you who supported me, I will soon add another game mode to it: [b]Ultimate Forget Total[/b], where the oldest 4th piece of the same type on the big board will dissapear, clearing all entries on the small board under it. This should be fun to play, and make for longer games. Not sure if I'll be able to implement it until the game's release date, but, if not, it will be available soon after, as an update to the base game.

Thank you all!
